### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **49** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**43** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2078e367430592f4808d70d2ca50ecdd75775ef`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **56** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2078e367430592f4808d70d2ca50ecdd75775ef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d8041d52ebf8e17065610ec064d30bd22b9b7b8d` — the merge of head `3eca62301806c15866bb0bb6dc5fbafd91af9061` into base `f2078e367430592f4808d70d2ca50ecdd75775ef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d8041d52ebf8e17065610ec064d30bd22b9b7b8d && git checkout d8041d52ebf8e17065610ec064d30bd22b9b7b8d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f2078e367430592f4808d70d2ca50ecdd75775ef 3eca62301806c15866bb0bb6dc5fbafd91af9061 && git checkout -B drift-repro f2078e367430592f4808d70d2ca50ecdd75775ef && git merge --no-ff 3eca62301806c15866bb0bb6dc5fbafd91af9061

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2078e367430592f4808d70d2ca50ecdd75775ef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f2078e367430592f4808d70d2ca50ecdd75775ef` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbWDsbbJizuYnDwBxT8

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `32a240bd7c83f803f2537d0bff30c99b4d710979`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #35144 (its body and all 11 comments, including the claim, the hand-on, seat ruling 6978086158, carry note 6980343159 and the four dev reports), the PR body, the 17-file list, the net diff `origin/main...32a240bd7c8` (merge base `ec227fc7b18`), the PR comments, the head's check-runs, and the round-4 merge's own resolutions (`git show --remerge-diff`). Code outside the diff was read at the head to judge the diff's claims, and was not reviewed: the engine's aggregate path, the SQL driver's aggregate compiler, the Turso driver, the `aggregate_records` handler with its helpers, both bridges with `callData`'s aggregate arm, the security middleware's aggregate input gate, and `withLookupGroupLabels`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`aggregate_records` accepts `orderBy` (up to 8 `{ field, order }` entries) and `limit` (a whole number from 1 to the row cap). Right.** Before this PR, the strict top-level door refused both keys as undeclared, so this widens the tool and refuses nothing it used to accept. The tool asks for `limit + 1` groups, so `truncated` reports a fact. An `orderBy` with no `limit` is cut at the cap and says so. These behaviours are pinned.
- **New aliases: `sort`, `sortBy`, `order` and `order_by` map to `orderBy`; `top`, `take` and `pageSize` map to `limit`. Right.** None of these names was taken on `main`. A scalar sent under `order` fails the array shape and is refused, so it is never misread.
- **The cut result is `{ rows, totalGroups, truncated?, currencies? }`. Right, and it matches seat ruling 6978086158 (Q2 = C).** `totalGroups` keeps its published meaning, the number of groups before the cut. On the cut path the statement's own `count(*) over ()` answers it. No `groupCount` appears in the result, the tool text, the changeset or the PR body, and the pins assert that it is absent on both paths.
- **The new refusals appear only on the new inputs. Right.** They are: `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`/501 for a bridge without the member; `INVALID_QUERY`/400 for a driver not on the compiling list, an aggregate computed in memory, a `having`, or a relation group; `INVALID_SORT`/400 for an order key that names no column of the aggregated row; and `INTERNAL_ERROR`/500 for rows that come back without the count. Each one is raised before the driver is asked, or before rows are served.
- **A call without the new arguments behaves exactly as on `main`. Right.** The default path's inline label call moved into the `labelServed` closure with the same arguments, and the served-schema read still happens after the aggregate. The diff shows no other change on that path.
- **`@objectstack/objectql` exports `AGGREGATE_ORDER_CUT` and the `AggregateOrderCutRequest`, `AggregateOrderKey` and `AggregateOrderCutOutcome` types. Right.** The option is a `Symbol.for` read option, so no JSON body or tool argument can carry it. The caller cannot supply `rank` either: the tool's `orderBy` entry drops any key it does not declare.
- **`engine.aggregate` serves the request only from inside `executeWithMiddleware`. Right.** It uses the `ast` that `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary` returns and the same `aggregateOptions` that the default native call uses. So the cut, the window count and the default path read the same rows under the same read filter, tenant wall and field gate. The order keys can name only columns of the aggregated row, which means aggregation aliases or group projections that the field-level input gate has already judged. `totalGroups` therefore counts only groups formed from rows the caller may read. The structure is right. Its pin is S3.
- **`driver-sql` wraps the grouped statement as a derived table, then applies `count(*) over ()` and `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` over the derived table's columns. Right.** NULLs rank last. An identity-folded measure (`sum` or a count) ranks as the `0` it is served as. Unnamed group keys break ties ascending. A key that names an unprojected column, or a malformed directive, is refused before the statement runs. The pins cover the statement, the tenant wall plus `where`, NULLs, the identity and rank.
- **The Turso driver's remote face refuses the directive. Its local and replica faces inherit the SQL driver. Right.** The engine checks drivers against a named list (`com.objectstack.driver.sql`, `com.objectstack.driver.sqlite-wasm`, and Turso only when `transportMode` is local or replica), and that list matches the drivers' own `name` and `transportMode` members. A driver missing from the list is refused, never served uncut.
- **`McpDataBridge.aggregateGroups` is a new optional member. Right.** Both implementers in the repo carry it, and the long-lived stdio wiring (`bridgeDataTools`) passes the bridge through unchanged. A bridge without the member keeps compiling and keeps serving `aggregate_records`, and the tool answers 501 for the new arguments. Both member-roster tripwires classify it.
- **`callData`'s aggregate arm returns `totalGroups` only when the in-process symbol is set, and refuses with a 500 when the engine does not report that the cut was served. Right.** Everything that runs before it still runs on both paths: the aggregation requirement, the relation-target exposure check and the internal-field door. The stdio bridge also runs the cut through the same `runAggregate` gates: the exposure whitelist, the relation-target exposure and the stored-metadata body and hash refusals.
- **Select-option order on a `limit`-only call: right.** Both paths derive it from one helper, `declaredOptionOrderKeys`, over `declaredOptionRank`, so the rule is not restated. The cut path sends it as `rank` keys, which the database takes before the cut. A caller's own `orderBy` reaches the bridge unchanged, and the explicit-order CONTROL pin shows it. Ties among undeclared values are S1.
- **Currency: right for fixed-mode amounts.** `fixedAmountCurrencies` is on the cut result, as on the uncut one, and is pinned. Record-mode ranking is S2.
- **Lookup-group labels: right, and carry 6980343159 is met.** The cut path calls the same `withLookupGroupLabels` through `labelServed`, with the same read-admission check (`readGuard`), on the rows served after the slice. The probe group is never labelled. One pin was added, and the label pins from #35202 remain in the file.
- **Round-4 merge resolutions keep both sides. Right.** The remerge diff shows three conflicts, all adjacent insertions: the bridge interface in `mcp-http-tools.ts`, the runtime HTTP bridge in `domains/mcp.ts`, and the write-response tripwire roster. Each kept both `aggregateGroups` and #35198's `userTextLocales`, with no hunk dropped from either side.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset gives `patch` to each of the five packages the diff moves: `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso` and `@objectstack/runtime`. That matches AGENTS.md: a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Nothing under `packages/spec` changes.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, because there is no authorable metadata key, value or type.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening: ...)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and it matches what the diff publishes. The diff adds two accepted tool arguments, aliases, an optional bridge member and an engine export, and refuses nothing that was accepted before. Following ruling 6978086158, the line no longer names `groupCount`, which is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Findings**

- S1 (should-fix) — A `rank` key does not order the values it leaves unlisted.
  - The engine appends only the group columns that the request does not name as ascending tie-breaks. A column named by a `rank` key is therefore excluded. In the driver, every value missing from the list falls into one `else n` arm and gets no ordering of its own.
  - Result: on a `limit`-only call over a select key whose data holds two or more undeclared values (a NULL among them), the order among those groups is not deterministic, and nor is which of them survives a cut at the boundary. This breaks the engine module's own claim that "two runs of one request answer the same groups in the same order". The driver's descending rank pin asserts only membership for that bucket.
  - Fix: keep a rank-keyed column in the trailing ascending tie-break (NULL last), or emit the column's own null-last ascending order right after the rank arm. Add a pin with two undeclared values at a cut boundary.
- S2 (should-fix) — Ordering by a record-mode amount ranks bare numbers across currencies.
  - The engine admits such a measure only when it is grouped by its currency-code field, so each row carries its code. Even so, the database ranks the bare numbers across currencies and cuts by them. A "top N by amount" over mixed currencies keeps the largest numbers, not the largest amounts, and drops the other groups without saying so. Before the cut, every group came back and could be compared by hand.
  - Fix, in increasing strength:
    1. State the rule in the tool description: rank a record-mode amount inside one currency, by filtering on the code field.
    2. Or refuse an order key over a record-mode amount alias unless `where` pins one currency.
  - Add a pin for whichever is chosen.
- S3 (should-fix) — The cut path has no pin that a read filter injected by middleware narrows both the cut and `totalGroups`.
  - The runtime end-to-end cells run as a system context. The driver cell covers the tenant wall and `where`, but no middleware-injected read scope.
  - The structure is right (see ①), and the new tool text advertises row-level security on this path, so the claim should be measured.
  - Fix: add one engine-level or runtime-level pin where a registered read middleware narrows `ast.where`, showing that the cut rows and `totalGroups` count only the admitted groups.
- N1 (nit) — The changeset says "A NULL ranks last in either direction", and its `rank` bullet says unlisted values rank "after" the listed ones. Under a descending rank key, both the unlisted values and the NULL come first; the driver pin shows this. The tool sends only `asc`, so the problem is latent. Correct the wording, or keep unlisted values last regardless of direction.
- N2 (nit) — The `orderBy` entry is an open `z.object`. An undeclared entry key is silently dropped, not refused, whereas the `aggregations` entries are closed at the producer (#28609). A caller-supplied `rank` is dropped either way, which is safe.
- N3 (nit) — `ORDER_RANK_MAX = 500` mirrors the engine's `AGGREGATE_ORDER_RANK_MAX`, but no pin ties the two values together, so drift would go undetected.
- N4 (nit) — In `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `STDIO_AGGREGATE_ORDER_CUT` sits between `unwrapRows`' docblock and the function, which leaves that docblock on the constant. The dev flagged this in round 3. Moving the constant above the docblock fixes it.

**SQL push-down (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 5)**

- The ordering, the cut and the group count run in one statement and one round trip: a derived table, a window count, `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT`, with the probe group as one extra row of the same statement.
- No in-memory fallback exists. Every path the database cannot serve is refused before the driver is asked, and named: other drivers, the in-memory tier, `having` and relation groups.
- Beyond the aggregate, the call reads the served schema once per call. Labels come from one batched read per referenced object, for the served ids only (#35202's existing shape).
- No query runs per row or per group. No finding.

**Answers to the dev reports**

- Round-1 `open_questions`:
  - Q1: answered by ruling 6978086158. `query_dataset` is split to #35194, and this PR says `Fixes #35144`.
  - Q2: answered by the same ruling (option C). `totalGroups` is kept and nothing else is added. Verified in ①.
  - Q3: answered by hand-on 6977042103 (option A) and implemented. One shared helper exists, the limit-only rank push-down is pinned and ablated, and `groups` and `totalGroups` stay on the default path.
- Hand-on items:
  - The explicit-order CONTROL pin: present.
  - `currencies` on the cut: present and pinned.
  - The `rows:` conflict: superseded by Q2 = C, with no `groupCount`.
- Carry note 6980343159: met (see ①).
- Deviations:
  - Round 1 (4), MySQL 8 or later for the window: accepted. On MySQL 5.7 the statement fails loudly and never returns a wrong answer, `driver-sql` already relies on window functions (`latest-per`), and the changeset states the requirement.
  - Round 2 (1), the Clause-② line rewritten to the ruling: correct.
  - Round 2 (3), unreleased internals renamed to `totalGroups`: accepted.
  - Round 3 (2), the `labelServed` closure: accepted, because it preserves the default path's behaviour.
  - The rest (vitest flag pass-through, trailer pair, single push, gate-union rerun, PR-body head notes) are process. None changes the contract.
- `out_of_scope_findings`:
  - The REST grouped-query arm (`orderBy` ignored, `limit` sliced in memory) is escalated to the seat. As reported, it is a Prime Directive 5 and Prime Directive 10 candidate with "carrier: none". It needs a measured repro and a card, or a recorded reason not to file one. It was not read here because it is outside this review's inputs.
  - The `objectstack-ask` SKILL.md follow-up is escalated to the seat to give it a carrier card.
  - The `unwrapRows` docblock placement is N4.
- `security_findings: none` is consistent with this read. The cut path reads as the caller through the same read admission, read scope and field gate as the default path, and it serves no group, count or label that the default path would not.

**Gates (check-runs at the head, read once at 16:47Z without waiting)**

- 25 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed.
- Still `in_progress`, with no verdict yet: Build Core, Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, and Type Check · workspace.
- This PASS is the contract record. Landing still waits for those 12 runs to turn green.

No must-fix. Should-fix: S1, S2, S3.

Reviewed-by: `area o1-C isolated reviewer (sub-agent of session_01JQwxbWDsbbJizuYnDwBxT8)`

**VERDICT: PASS**

repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbWDsbbJizuYnDwBxT8

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3eca62301806c15866bb0bb6dc5fbafd91af9061`
Local-runs: none

This is a DELTA review over PASS record 6985265817 at `32a240bd7c83f803f2537d0bff30c99b4d710979`. Everything that record judged and the delta does not touch stands as it was judged there.

Read: record 6985265817, head note 6987666833 on this PR, dev report 6987634040 on card #35144, the PR body at this head, the delta `32a240bd7c8..3eca6230180` (two commits, 9 files, +205/-56), and the head's check-runs. Code outside the delta was read at the head to judge the delta's claims, and was not reviewed: the rest of the engine's order-cut module (the shape check and its rank limit), the SQL driver's order-cut statement builder, and the tool's declared-option rank helpers (`declaredOptionOrderKeys`, `declaredOptionOrderBy`, `inDeclaredOptionOrder`). The dev report and head note cite a review addendum for N3 and the changeset's `KEY__label` clause. That addendum is not among this review's inputs, so both are judged against the code only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1 is closed. Right.** In `aggregateOrderCutDirective`, the only behaviour change in the delta, a column named only by a `rank` key no longer counts as named. It therefore stays among the trailing ascending keys, and the driver orders a trailing key null-flag first, then by value, so NULL comes last. Every group column now appears in the full order as a plain key, which makes the order total on every path, the ranked bucket included. Two runs of one call answer the same groups, and the module's own determinism claim holds again.
  - The pin would go red without the fix. The runtime real-SQLite cell cuts inside the unlisted bucket and asserts the cut membership, the same answer on a second run, the full order with NULL last, and the statement's null-last ascending tie-break after the CASE. The engine and stdio directive pins assert the ranked column among the trailing keys.
  - The dev ablated the one engine line. On the second, valid attempt, all three pins went red, and the runtime cell's received order shows SQLite really did keep a NULL group inside the cut. The dev reports the first attempt as a no-op that read green, and says so. That disclosure is right.
- **Deviation (3): with several group keys, the ranked column joins the trailing keys in `groupBy` order. Accepted.** The tool sends rank keys only for a leading run of option keys (`declaredOptionOrderKeys` stops at the first key that is not one), so no unnamed key ever precedes a ranked one on the tool's path. Determinism does not depend on the position, because every group column is in the order. With two or more leading rank keys, the wording is slightly too broad (nit n1).
- **S2 is closed by option 1, the seat's choice. Right.** The `aggregate_records` description now states that ranking a per-record-currency amount compares bare numbers across currencies, and that the ranking belongs inside one currency, filtered by `where` on the code field. No refusal was added, so nothing accepted before is refused. The `tools/list` pin matches the exact sentence, so it goes red if the sentence is removed or changed. The changeset gains a matching bullet.
- **S3 is closed. Right.** A runtime real-SQLite describe block registers a read middleware that narrows `ast.where`. It asserts that the cut rows and `totalGroups` count only the admitted groups, that one grouped statement carries the window, and, in a CONTROL, that the uncut aggregate through the same middleware agrees. The pin discriminates: if the cut read the pre-middleware AST, both the cut's members and `totalGroups` would differ from the asserted values. The CONTROL also proves that the middleware itself takes effect, so the cell cannot pass because of a middleware that never runs. There is no code change, consistent with record 6985265817 finding the structure right.
- **N1 is closed. Right.** The changeset, the engine docblocks, the driver comments and the PR body now say what the driver does:
  - On a key without a `rank`, NULL ranks last in either direction.
  - Under a rank, every unlisted value, NULL included, shares one rank past the listed values. So the unlisted values come after the listed ones under an ascending rank and before them under a descending rank.
  - Inside that bucket, the trailing ascending keys order the values, NULL last, in both directions.

  These statements match the CASE arm (`else n`, with `order` applied over the ranks) and the trailing-key arm in the driver.
- **N3 is closed, with a behavioural pin instead of an export (deviation 2). Accepted.** Exporting `AGGREGATE_ORDER_RANK_MAX` would publish a new engine export, and this round was not ordered to make that change. The stdio-over-real-engine cell covers both sides of the boundary:
  - A declared list at the limit is sent as a rank and served.
  - One value past the limit, the tool sends no rank, and the engine refuses that rank before the driver is asked.

  Each one-sided drift goes red: the tool raising or lowering its limit alone, or the engine doing so alone. The refusal arm asserts only the code and status (nit n2).
- **N4 is closed. Right.** Each `Symbol.for` constant in `stdio-data-bridge.ts` now carries its own docblock, and `unwrapRows` carries its own. Deviation (1), moving #35199's `STDIO_LATEST_PER` with ours, is placement only: the value and spelling are unchanged. The conflict this move creates with the draft #35225 is an adjacent insertion, a landing-order matter rather than a contract matter.
- **Nothing else in the delta changes behaviour.**
  - The driver hunks are comments.
  - The tool hunk is one description sentence.
  - The second commit types the N3 pin's engine call. The query-options-erasure surface is back at its ceiling, and its CI lane is green.
  - The test harness refactor (`boot` and a `def` parameter on `makeStdio`) is test-only.
- **The changeset's new `KEY__label` clause matches the code that record 6985265817 judged.** The cut path labels lookup and master-detail group keys through the same label helper, reading as the caller, on the served rows only. N2 was skipped as ordered.
- **Read-as-caller is not weakened.** The only new order key is a group column the statement already projects and the field gate has already judged. The delta adds no read, column, label source or count path. The row filter, `totalGroups` and labels reach the cut exactly as before, and S3 now measures the row filter and `totalGroups`.
